description.narrative: The National Coalition of Human Rights Defenders - Kenya (NCHRD eller Defenders Coalition) är en medlemsorganisation etablerad 2007 och registrerad i Kenya som en stiftelse. Defenders Coalition arbetar primärt med skydd av människorättsförsvarare i Kenya. Bland annat innebär deras arbete att starka kapaciteten av människorättsförsvarare för att arbeta mer effektivt, samtidigt som de arbetar med påverkansarbete för bättre lagstiftning och institutionell miljö för att minska människorättsförsvarare sårbarhet för förföljelse och/eller skada. Ambassaden bidrar med kärnstöd till Defenders Coalition Strategiska Plan 2022-2025 - Safety. Security. Wellbeing of Rights Defenders.

The National Coalition of Human Rights Defenders - Kenya (NCHRD or Defenders Coalition) is a national membership organization established in 2007 and registered under Kenyan law as a Trust. The Defenders Coalition works primarily for the protection of Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) in Kenya. Among others, the Defenders Coalition strengthens capacities of HRDs to work more effectively, besides advocating for favorable legal, policy and institutional environments in order to reduce their vulnerability to the risk of persecution and or harm. The Embassy provide core-support to the Defenders Coalition Strategic Plan 2020-2025 - Safety. Security. Wellbeing of Rights Defenders.

The overall objective is Enhancing the Safety, Security and Wellbeing of Human Rights Defenders.
Key results areas and specific objectives are:
I. Supportive and enabling norms, policies and institutional frameworks that enhance security, work and wellbeing of HRDs adopted
Objective 1: To influence the development of new legislation and policy solutions for protecting human rights defenders including environmental, women, indigenous people, youth, PWDs, journalists & LGBTQI from retaliation, by building the capacity of HRDs and their allies to conduct effective legislative advocacy campaigns and fostering collaborative networks.
Objective 2: To contribute to enhanced enabling environment/ civic space for HRDs through promoting positive public perceptions/attitude change towards HRDs and their work
II. Effective protection response to and safe working envrionment for diverse HRDs at risk delivered in a timely and appropriate manner
Objective: To improve the provision of sustainable & effective services for human rights defenders through building the capacity of legal professionals through skills building and supporting legal professionals engaging in strategic litigation.
III. Socie-economic wellbeing for HRDs improved for increased civic engagement, passionate and accountable protection for human rights
Objective: To promote awareness on mental health to eliminate stigma and encourage HRDs to seek interventions and promote social recognition and celebration of the work and resilience of HRDs.
IV. Defenders Coalition consolidates its position as a 'dynamic, relevant, effective and resilient institution'
Objective: To strengthen the institutional capacity to implement its mandate efficiently and effectively through strengthening of internal systems and structures.
The key results areas are consistent with the Defenders Coalition Strategi Plan 2020-2025

The Defenders Coalition reported realization of remarkable achievements during the period January to December 2025, owing to the efforts and resources invested over a period of time. Some of the key milestones reported in each of the strategic focus areas are as follows:
Outcome 1: Supportive and enabling norms, policies and institutional frameworks that enhance security, work and wellbeing of HRDs adopted.
Objective 1: To influence the development of new legislation and policy solutions for protecting human rights defenders including environmental, women, indigenous people, youth, PWDs, journalists & LGBTQI from retaliation, by building the capacity of HRDs and their allies to conduct effective legislative advocacy campaigns and fostering collaborative networks.
Objective 2: To contribute to enhanced enabling environment/ civic space for HRDs through promoting positive public perceptions/attitude change towards HRDs and their work.
Key results under this outcome area:
1. Strengthened Legislative and Policy Advocacy Capacity of human rights defenders (HRDs).
- Defenders Coalition enhanced the advocacy skills of 15 HRDs through a comprehensive Training of Trainers (ToT) on legislative advocacy. HRDs gained practical tools to analyze power dynamics, map stakeholders, develop community-level advocacy strategies, and effectively engage regional and international human rights mechanisms such as the Universal Periodic Report (UPR), African Commission on Human and People's Rights (ACHPR), and UN Special Procedures. This significantly improved their confidence and ability to influence policy and legal reforms.
2. Enhanced Collaboration and Dialogue Between HRDs and Duty Bearers.
- Through county-level engagement forums in counties like Samburu and Kilifi, the Coalition improved the relationship between grassroots HRDs and local authorities. Tangible results included joint human rights initiatives, faster response to HRD concerns, and the inclusion of HRDs in Court Users Committeesstrengthening mechanisms for justice, accountability, and protection at the community level.
3. Stronger Regional and International Advocacy for Protection of Civic Space.
- The Coalition actively engaged in key regional and international mechanisms, including the 80th and 81st ACHPR sessions and the 2025 UPR process. It co-drafted national and joint civil society reports, highlighted civic space violations in Kenya, and advanced recommendations on freedoms of assembly, association, expression, and HRD protection. These engagements amplified HRD voices at global platforms and pushed for legal and policy reforms.
4. Improved Public Perception and Visibility of HRDs Through National Recognition Initiatives.
- The 2024 Human Rights Defenders Awards successfully celebrated and profiled 14 outstanding HRDs, supported by extensive mainstream and community media coverage (17 media features and 12 radio engagements). The awards attracted 512 participants and saw an increase in nominations compared to 2023, enhancing public appreciation of HRDs and promoting positive narratives around their work. Additional sensitization initiatives, including International Womens Day events addressing technology facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), further strengthened public awareness of HRD issues.
Outcome 2: Effective protection response to and safe working environment for diverse HRDs at risk delivered in a timely and appropriate manner.
Objective 2: To improve the provision of sustainable & effective services for human rights defenders through building the capacity of legal professionals through skills building and supporting legal professionals engaging in strategic litigation.
Key results under this outcome area:
1. Large-Scale, Timely Protection Support Reaching HRDs at Risk Nationwide.
- 2,239 HRDs and organizations received direct protection assistance.
- 1,715 HRDs received legal representation, preventing wrongful convictions and judicial harassment.
- 288 HRDs supported with bail/bond, enabling them to continue their work while facing charges.
- 98 HRDs safely relocated from imminent threats, averting severe harm or death.
- 6 HRD organizations strengthened their physical/digital security; 15 HRDs received legal accompaniment.
- Surge in risks documented, including 58 Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity/Expression (SOGIE) HRDs attacked, signaling worsening operating environment.
- Development of a comprehensive protection policy, institutionalizing risk assessments and emergency response systems.
2. Rapid Fact-Finding and Crisis Response in Emerging Human Rights Situations.
- Kargi fact-finding mission (Marsabit) uncovered systemic failures in police response to brutal attacks on two women; issued recommendations on prosecution and community sensitization.
- Six flood-related fact-finding missions across five regions assessed destruction, risks, and humanitarian gaps.
- Emergency support delivered to 18 HRD households, 5 Social Justice Centres, 2 SOGIE organizations, and 8 individual HRDs affected by floods.
- Additional medical and economic recovery assistance provided, including business recovery in Kitengela.
3. Strengthened National Protection Ecosystem and Coordination.
- Three Protection Working Group (PWG) meetings convened, enhancing collective analysis of HRD risks and coordinated response.
- Joint monitoring with Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) ensured rapid identification of threats and improved rescue and support pathways for at-risk HRDs.
4. Increased Solidarity, Visibility, and Justice for HRDs and HRD Networks.
- Solidarity visit to Wongan Women Initiative (Marsabit) amplified indigenous women HRDs climate justice work and strengthened partnerships with multiple national/international actors.
- Justice secured in the Elizabeth Ekaru murder case33-year sentence for the perpetratorfollowing sustained legal, advocacy, and security support to the family and local HRDs.
- Marked progress in combating impunity for violence against women HRDs and reinforcing state accountability.
5. Enhanced Safety and Security Skills of HRDs and HRDOs.
- Security management trainings delivered to HRDs from nine counties and 22 organizational leaders, improving risk assessment, security planning, and digital safety practices.
- MDR training for Women HRDs in Isiolo and Marsabit strengthened documentation and reporting of human rights and climate-related violations.
- Three bi-monthly HRD Working Group meetings (with diplomatic partners) deepened collective understanding of civic space dynamics and HRD safety priorities.
- Active participation in SOGIE National Strategic Working Group and lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, or queer (LGBTQ) Technical Working Groups, contributing to contextual analysis, security responses, and advocacy planning.
Outcome 3: Socie-economic wellbeing for HRDs improved for increased civic engagement, passionate and accountable protection for human rights.
Objective: To promote awareness on mental health to eliminate stigma and encourage HRDs to seek interventions and promote social recognition and celebration of the work and resilience of HRDs.
Key Results under this outcome area:
1. Strengthened HRD Capacity and Nationwide Solidarity Through the 9th HRD Academy.
- Delivered Kenyas largest annual HRD capacity-building event, convening 171 participants (150 HRDs from all 47 counties, including women human rights defenders (WHRDs), SOGIE activists, minority groups, artivists).
- Strengthened HRDs socio-economic and advocacy resilience through training on digital security, civic space compliance, ecological justice, first aid, and psychosocial well-being.
- Reinforced national solidarity and recognition of HRDs through the HRD Awards 2024, gala events, and peer-learning exchanges.
2. Enhanced Economic Empowerment and Financial Resilience of HRDs
- Trained 50 Social Justice Centre finance officers from 8 counties on financial literacy, bookkeeping, compliance, procurement, and risk mitigationclosing major capacity gaps and strengthening institutional accountability.
- Supported 170 HRDs to showcase income-generating activities at the HRD Academy exhibition, expanding market linkages, direct sales, and visibility for HRD-led enterprises.
3. Strengthened WHRD Networks and Collective Advocacy on Gender Justice
- Convened WHRDs from all 47 counties under the Ni Mama Network, equipping them with practical tools to prevent and respond to technology-facilitated GBV and shaping a framework for engagement with the National Police Service.
- Contributed to national momentum on ending femicide, participating in the End Femicide Leaders Workshop and amplifying advocacy that led to the establishment of a Presidential Technical Working Group.
4. Prioritized Mental Health and Psychosocial Support for HRDs Across the Country
- Conducted Mental Health Day events in 6 counties, benefiting 180 HRDs with counselling, stress-management training, and accessible mental-health resources in multiple languages.
- Delivered four targeted debrief sessions (post-floods responders, Mothers of Victims network, Uyombo LEDs, Mukuru SJC), supporting over 90 HRDs to process trauma, reduce burnout, and strengthen resilience.
- Continued collective solidarity efforts through civic events like the Mashujaa Festival, despite repression, reinforcing HRDs emotional strength and commitment.
Outcome 4: Defenders Coalition consolidates its position as a dynamic, relevant, effective and resilient institution.
Objective 4: To strengthen the institutional capacity to implement its mandate efficiently and effectively through strengthening of internal systems and structures.
Key results under this outcome area:
1. Strengthened Governance and Institutional Systems.
- Developed and/or revised core governance and operational frameworks, including the Procurement Policy, Board Manual, standard operating procedures (SOPs), Finance Policy, Safeguarding Policy, and other regulatory documents.
- The Board held four quarterly meetings and an annual retreat, leading to the formulation and adoption of six new organisational policies.
- These reforms enhanced transparency, accountability, internal controls, and decision-making.
2. Enhanced Organisational Efficiency and Strategic Management.
- Annual Operational Plans (AOPs) improved strategic alignment, planning discipline, and resource utilisation, enabling clearer tracking of results.
- Quarterly reviews, digital system upgrades, and procurement of essential office equipment strengthened operational agility and organisational resilience.
- The organisation also advanced digital transformation, including expansion of the Case Intake digital platform and Mtetezi documentation system.
3. Improved Staff Capacity, Welfare, and Performance Culture.
- Expanded human resource capacity through the recruitment of five new staff, establishment of middle-level management, and implementation of internal promotions.
- Introduced or maintained staff medical, group life, and work injury benefits Act (WIBA) insurance, contributing to high motivation, retention, and wellbeing.
- Conducted a two-day staff retreat, annual appraisals, and targeted professional development, strengthening team cohesion, leadership, and performance.
4. Strengthened Financial Stewardship and Sustainability Efforts.
- Successfully completed an external financial audit with an unqualified opinion, demonstrating strong financial integrity and compliance with donor standards.
- Developed management action plans to address audit recommendations, improving risk management and financial oversight.
- Advanced sustainability through the Climb for Justice fundraising campaign, mobilising public participation and generating diversified support.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
